spec_match.rationale: The linter implements spec 6.4 rule-for-rule (iamf prefix, 3-digit 0-255 profiles, four substream codecs matched case-insensitively, mp4a locked to 40.2), mirrored against Chromium's ParseIamfCodecId, and pairs it with real isTypeSupported/decodingInfo calls.

interactive.rationale: Free-text input plus eight preset buttons that run the lint immediately; every run renders the per-rule trace and the browser's live answers.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index card promises rule-level malformed-string diagnosis compared against the real browser verdict; the page renders exactly that comparison.

edge_cases.rationale: This IS the edge concept: non-3-digit profiles, out-of-range 999, foreign codec ec-3, HE-AAC mp4a.40.5, trailing elements, and the bare-iamf Chromium test-only quirk each produce a distinct named failure, and the page states plainly when browser answers cannot separate valid from malformed.

references.rationale: Links ChromeStatus, spec section 6.4, and the Chromium audio_codecs.cc source.

conformance.rationale: The suite's malformed-profile-digits and foreign-substream assertions pin the same rejection contract with tests that could genuinely fail on a claiming browser; 8/8 pass in the verification browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP-driven headless Chromium 141 exercised four presets through the real buttons: valid Opus (grammar VALID, browser honestly unsupported with the cannot-distinguish note), 999 profile and mp4a.40.5 (INVALID with the exact broken rule, consistent rejection), bare iamf (test-only-quirk branch); console/network clean.

telemetry_health.rationale: iamf-lint-ran asserts each complete run; iamf-lint-no-invalid-accepted fires on grammar-invalid strings and genuinely fails if a browser claims support for one.

design_system.rationale: Preset buttons override background AND color together (ivory/black); rule marks use the darkened emerald and rose on ivory; all colours are variables.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled text input, preset group with role=group and aria-label, rule marks paired with full sentence text, and a role=status live region for the verdict.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Measured scrollWidth 360 at 360x740 DPR3 with panels stacking via auto-fit minmax; desktop verified via responsive-check.

openQuestions.title: Confirm the bare-iamf quirk branch on an IAMF-enabled build
openQuestions.detail: On enabled builds Chromium accepts bare 'iamf' (test-only, per the ParseIamfCodecId comment). The page has a dedicated verdict branch for that state but it has only executed the both-false path here. Re-run the preset on an enabled build to see the quirk branch live.

guidanceConsulted.query: form validation inline error messaging accessibility
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Error feedback should be programmatically announced once, tied to the interaction, not per-fragment.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The per-rule trace renders silently and the single role=status verdict line announces the outcome after each lint run.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: CDP run: status text updates once per preset press

guidanceConsulted.query: async feature detection status updates aria live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Do not communicate pass/fail by glyph or colour alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Every ✓/✕ mark is followed by a full-sentence explanation of the rule outcome in text.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Rule list text verified in CDP DOM output

summary: Edge/failure angle: spec 6.4 grammar as an interactive rule-by-rule linter beside the browser's real rejection, honest about what a no-IAMF browser can and cannot distinguish, including Chromium's documented bare-iamf test quirk. Verified via CDP-driven headless Chromium 141 (sanctioned cloud fallback) across valid, out-of-range, wrong-mp4a, and bare presets; clean console/network.
